description:
In this episode of “I’d Like to Know”, Pastors Stephen Bohr  and David Salazar dive into a complex and often misunderstood issue:

🔍 Should Seventh-day Adventists purchase life insurance?

Drawing from Ellen G. White’s statements in Testimonies Vol. 1 (pages 549–551), the pastors examine:

What did EGW really mean by saying life insurance was “not approved of God”?

Does the EGW Estate’s modern explanation effectively deconstruct this view?

Is "providing for the future" more about living within one’s means and saving, or about trusting life insurance payouts?

How do the “Brother’s Keeper” principles in 1T 113–115 reshape our understanding of insurance and stewardship among Adventists?

🩺 The conversation also touches on health insurance and how Ellen White’s guidance may apply given the SDA Church’s vast medical infrastructure today.

📖 Whether you're an Adventist curious about financial responsibility or a researcher diving into EGW writings, this episode offers deep, biblical clarity.

📅 New episodes every Tuesday at 4PM PT on SUMtv.
